question: If three cards are drawn one by one randomly from a pack of 52 cards, then what is the probability that three of them are jack?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Jacks** in a deck = 4. Total cards = 52.

Probability for 1st Jack = 4/52. Probability for 2nd Jack = 3/51. Probability for 3rd Jack = 2/50.

Required Probability = (4 × 3 × 2) ÷ (52 × 51 × 50)

Simplified Result = 1 ÷ (13 × 17 × 25) = 1/5525.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0433a1eafcacefd5939df80b85ec229ccb2ea47799b3ffef3d3bea9af734f9b.png] 

**Given:** Total cards = 52, Number of Jacks = 4.

**Formula:** Probability P(E) = n(E) ÷ n(S) or ⁿCᵣ method.

⇒ Total ways to draw 3 cards = ⁵²C₃

⇒ Favorable ways to draw 3 Jacks = ⁴C₃

⇒ Required Probability = ⁴C₃ ÷ ⁵²C₃

⇒ Required Probability = 4 ÷ [(52 × 51 × 50) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1)]

⇒ Required Probability = (4 × 6) ÷ (52 × 51 × 50)

⇒ Required Probability = 24 ÷ 132600

⇒ Required Probability = 1/5525

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combinations Formula

The number of ways to select r items from n is ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r! × (n−r)!].

Deck Composition

A standard deck has 52 cards: 4 suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) with 13 cards each, including 4 **Face Cards** of each type (King, Queen, Jack).

Multiplication Rule

For dependent events (without replacement), P(A and B and C) = P(A) × P(B|A) × P(C|A and B).</p
